about: One job per page (Ben, 10:27, product/words.md: "each page should have one purpose"). Read by scripts/page-jobs.mjs from app-check on every route. first: what must be wholly on the first screen, above the tab bar, in the typical world (a CSS selector on the web render). title: the words the page opens with. sections: the most section headers the whole page may have. never: parts that belong on another page, with where they go. Why each is so: features/app/page-jobs.md.

(tabs)/index.job: Clear what needs you, the most urgent first.
(tabs)/index.title: today

(tabs)/sell.job: See everything you sell by where it is, and open one.
(tabs)/sell.title: sell

(tabs)/buy.job: Find a thing, or see what your searches found.
(tabs)/buy.title: buy

(tabs)/you.job: See how you are doing at a glance, and get to each thing about you.
(tabs)/you.title: you

item/[id]/index.job: One thing: where it is, and its next step.

search.job: Find one thing across every site.

worth.job: Know what a thing is worth, then decide to sell or keep it.

want.job: Say what you are looking for, and how much you would pay.

camera.job: Get a thing in, one photo at a time.
